caption: That Halloween scare filter is a lot less funny when the kid isn’t in on the joke.   Most preschoolers can tell pretend from real after age 3, but they need support to understand the difference before they understand on their own. The catch is that fear makes it hard for them to hold onto that in the moment. So your kiddo might “know” monsters aren’t real and still panic when one lunges at them.   With Halloween coming up, a few small things can make it way more likely your child has fun instead of spending the night clinging to your leg.   🎃 Play with masks before the big night. Put one on, take it off, and say “it’s just me under here.” That on-off game builds trust fast. 🎃 Go visit scary and not scary halloween decorations WITH them. Point out things. My daughter was afraid of an animatronic spider, but we went up to it together, touched it, and I showed her it wasn't real. I didn't pretend to be scared, scream, or scare her. The scaring can come when they understand PRETEND more. 🎃 When they get scared, avoid “don’t be scared.” Try “that looked scary, I’m right here.”   This week’s Happy, Pappy? episode is a sweet way to talk with kids about fear, and reality versus pretend One line I want every kid to hear: being brave doesn’t mean pretending you’re not scared.
